items.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022
items.q: Shecky said to me one night, he says, “I’ve walked out on several comics that were too dirty for me.”

ctx.x: I heard you say something about seeing Shecky Greene for the first time and you were amazed that he had no structure or beginning or ending and still he was hilarious.

I mean I laughed so hard that I was ill. I had no idea. And it was sort of a revelation to me because I had been working in Chicago with a group, the group The Millionaires, and we were there for about six months at one club, it was a really good gig. And older guys, comics, would come in. They started to come in and word was spreading there’s this © Fillius Jazz Archive -7-

comic working at the Cairo Club. And so then the guys say, “You remind us of Shecky Greene” and I never heard his name before because he wasn’t a TV comic you know. I said, “Who is that?” And they said, “Oh he’s out in Vegas, he’s making big money, he’s doing real good.” I said, “Oh great.” And so I went to see Shecky, I heard all about him, he was a legend out here, I mean truly a legend, partly because of his wild antics. Shecky found out he was clinically depressed and when he’d drink he would do things, you…
